questions.question: The plan wires check_repo_traps.py into `lint` only. In CI, `lint` runs only when a diff matches CODE_PAT, but rule 1 (invisible characters) reads every file git lists, including sdd/, docs-src/, CHANGELOG.md. A PR touching only those runs `docs-gate`, not `lint`, so CI would not catch a U+2028 landing there. The repo's standing pattern for such checks (check-traces, check-no-retrospective, …) is a standalone alias wired into both. Which wiring?

options.label: lint + docs-gate (Recommended)
options.description: Add a `check-repo-traps` alias and put it in `docs-gate` too, with the usual pyproject comment naming the CODE_PAT/DOCS_PAT reason. CI then reaches rule 1 for docs-only diffs. Paths matching neither pattern (e.g. .claude/hooks/) stay a stated bound.

options.label: lint only, as planned
options.description: Keep the plan. State in the docstring bounds that an sdd/- or docs-only diff skips the check in CI; local `fast` and `all` still run it.

Rule 1 would fail lint on a decision log under sdd/decisions/ whose recorded dialog text carries e.g. a U+2028 or NBSP (record_decision.py writes ensure_ascii=False by design). Which fix?

options.label: Exclude sdd/decisions/ (Recommended)
options.description: Rule 1 skips that directory, stated as a bound in the docstring and pinned by a test seen failing first. The log stays a record 'stored as received'; rule 1 keeps guarding authored files. Small, contained to this PR's script.

options.label: Recorder writes ensure_ascii=True
options.description: Logs hold \uXXXX escapes instead of raw characters, so rule 1 never sees one and diffs show them. Touches record_decision.py, check_traces.py's raw-separator comment and its tests: a second mechanism changed in this PR. Existing logs keep raw non-ASCII (none from the 21 today).

questions.question: Round 7's finding 2: the hand-written .gitattributes matcher still differs from git (core.ignorecase=true here, so `*.png binary` covers LOGO.PNG for git but not for us; quoted/escaped patterns; nested .gitattributes). `git check-attr -z --stdin binary` takes 0.020s over all 2250 listed files and handles all of it. Which way?

options.label: Ask git (check-attr) (Recommended)
options.description: Replace binary_patterns, _attr_regex, _bracket_class, _POSIX_CLASSES and _is_binary (~90 lines) with one check-attr call. Drops two stated bounds (nested files, case folding) and the code that drew rounds 4 and 5. Tests that wrote .gitattributes without a repo get a `git init`; the bracket/slash cases stay as behaviour tests against git.

options.label: Keep the matcher, add case folding
options.description: Fold case when `git config core.ignorecase` is true and state quoted/escaped patterns and nested files as bounds. Smaller diff; keeps a second implementation of git's rules that review has found wanting three rounds running.

Ruff 0.15.13's PLE2502 flags U+200F RIGHT-TO-LEFT MARK and U+061C ARABIC LETTER MARK, neither in the gate's 21; U+200E LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK is the third directional mark, which ruff skips. None occurs in the 2182 files rule 1 reads. How should the set change?

options.label: Add all three marks (Recommended)
options.description: 24 code points: U+061C, U+200E, U+200F join the set, the test literal and the dossier plan. Then the plan's 'PLE would be a second driver for a subset' is true (PLE2502 ⊆ ours), and 'bidi controls' covers every directional mark, not only those ruff names.

options.label: Add ruff's two only
options.description: 23 code points: U+061C and U+200F. The subset claim becomes exactly true; U+200E stays out, with the reason stated.

options.label: Keep 21, fix the sentence
options.description: No code change; the dossier states that PLE2502 also flags U+061C and U+200F and that they are deliberately out. The gate's 'bidi controls' wording is narrowed to the embedding/override/isolate controls.
